_source: build-doc §9.7 asset manifest · §9.1 pipeline · §9.2 locked generation parameters · §9.3 post-process chain · §8.4 style lock. Rows carry id, class, subject string, view, seed, target size and status exactly as §9.7 specifies.
_derivation: rows[] IS DERIVED — never hand-edited. `npx tsx tools/comfy/comfy-batch.ts rebuild` regenerates every row from data/species.json, data/gyms.json, data/nodes/*.json, core/types.ts PROP_KINDS and the authored blocks below, and tests/unit/manifest.test.ts fails if the committed rows differ from a fresh derivation. That is the G2 gate: a species, node or gym leader cannot exist in the manifest without existing in data/, and cannot exist in data/ without appearing here.
_authoredBlocks: Everything prefixed `_` below is AUTHORED CONTENT, transcribed from docs/content-bible.md with a per-entry source. It lives here rather than in data/ because data/ is Lane A's and carries no art copy; it is the art lane's transcription of the bible, subject to G2 exactly as data/ is.
_seedRule: seed = pin ?? hashSeed(version, id) using core/rng.ts's FNV-1a (§8.1's own hash — no second generator, G11). A row's seed is therefore a pure function of its id and its version, which is what makes G5 mechanical: regenerating an asset re-derives the SAME seed, and the only way to get a different one is to bump `version`, which is the manifest-entry versioning §8.4 licenses. `recordedSeed` freezes the seed actually used the first time a row produced a file; the runner refuses to submit a different seed for that row unless the version moved (SeedReuseError).

_credits._source: build-doc §9.1 / G13 — a projected credit estimate and an explicit --confirm before any batch ≥ 20 rows.
_credits._finding: Comfy Cloud exposes NO credit-balance endpoint (/api/customers/credit, /api/credit, /api/user/credit all 404), so the estimate cannot be read from the API. It is a measured per-image figure or it is nothing.
_credits.measuredFrom: Dashboard delta, 2026-08-26. cloud.comfy.org account menu read 4,147 before the first trial and 4,127 after 18 generations at 1024x1024 — 20 credits / 18 images = 1.11, recorded as 1.12 so the projection rounds against us. Read from the UI because Comfy Cloud exposes no credit endpoint (see _finding). A later reading over a mixed batch that included 256x256 health probes came out near 0.53 per image, so 1.12 is the 1024x1024 figure and small probes cost materially less.
_credits.note: null means UNCALIBRATED. The runner still refuses a ≥20-row batch without --confirm; it prints the row count and states plainly that the per-image cost has never been measured, rather than inventing a number. Supply --credits-per-image=N (read off the dashboard before/after a known batch) and the runner records it here.
_credits._dryRunNote: `--credits-per-image=N` prints the calibrated projection but does not persist on a --dry-run, so this pair was written directly. The number is the measurement above, not an estimate — G13 forbids inventing one.

_deviations.finding: 154 battle sprites is arithmetically impossible against the shipped roster. data/species.json holds 27 lines of which 3 are Ancients; 24 aging lines × 3 age forms + 3 Ancients × 1 form = 75 forms × front/back = 150.
_deviations.action: The manifest derives 150 creature-battle rows from data/species.json. §9.7's 154 is the number an art reviewer counts against, so the gap is stated here rather than discovered mid-review.

_deviations.finding: rembg is a Python/ONNX salient-object segmenter; it is not installed, it is not deterministic across versions, and it is not idempotent — a second pass re-mattes an already-matted sprite.
_deviations.action: Background removal is a border flood fill against the flat generated background key. Every prompt ends in `plain white background` (the §9.2 skeleton, verbatim), so the background is a known flat key, not an unknown photograph. The fill is exact, deterministic and idempotent, which is what §9.3's own 'every step idempotent' clause requires and what §10.4's idempotency test measures. If a class ever generates on a non-flat background, that class needs a real matte and this note is where to start.

_deviations.finding: §9.3's chain starts at 'nearest-neighbour downscale to target'. The raw outputs are 1024² frames containing a subject that occupies a fraction of the canvas; downscaling that to 96² yields a creature ~20px tall floating in white.
_deviations.action: A trim-to-content step runs BEFORE step 1 for the sprite classes (declared per class as `postprocess.trim`), and the downscale then fits the trimmed subject into the target frame preserving aspect. §9.3's three named steps keep their order and their semantics; this is an addition, not a reordering. Maps and painted dex do not trim.

_deviations.finding: Two post-process target sizes named in §9.3 — battle 96² and mini 32² — have no home in data/balance.json, unlike the overworld character size (balance.map.playerSpriteW/H), the map size (balance.map.mapNativePx) and the prop scale (balance.map.propInteractionRadiusDefault).
_deviations.action: They ship as `targetW`/`targetH` on the class specs in this file, which is the art lane's data file. tests/unit/manifest.test.ts binds every class target that DOES have a balance source to that source, so the three sizes that are shared with the game can never drift; the two that are art-only are reviewable in one place. Raised for Lane A: `balance.map.battleSpritePx` and `balance.map.miniSpritePx` would close it.

_deviations.finding: Seven of the 35 dex identities have no concept text anywhere in the bible: Vulkindle, Pyrevane, Rillisk, Maelstrisk, Bramblore, Thornwald (the metamorphic starters' adult/elder identities) and — partially — Gloomgrub.
_deviations.action: Handled the way every other number the bible leaves open is handled: BY PUBLISHED RULE, not by taste. A form with no concept of its own inherits its line's bible concept plus its age stage ('grown to its adult form'). No new anatomy, colour or creature is invented; the entry records `derivedFrom` and its rule so a reviewer can audit it in one place. Gloomgrub's concept IS bible-sourced (§4 row 16 and the metamorphic paragraph: 'Poison/Plant grub').

The build needs five more: route maps, environment props, UI frames, the painted dex class (§9.4, untrialed by design) and img2img year variants (§9.5, untrialed).

_deviations.finding: bible §6 gives an aging arc for each of the 6 towns/sites and NONE for the 6 routes, but §9.5 needs an arc string per node to append to the year-variant prompt.
_deviations.action: A route inherits the aging arc of the town that shares its biome (R1↔Hearthollow Meadow, R2↔Brackwater Marsh, R3↔Bowerdeep Forest, R4↔Cindershelf Steppe, R5↔Duskhollow Vale, Sanctum Approach↔The Sanctum Fallow). _deviations.finding: L6 says the string `green shirt, ranger cap with star badge, leather satchel, walking boots` appears VERBATIM in every player prompt. The prompt that actually produced the gate-B0-approved sprite does not contain it verbatim — it elaborates: `a green shirt, brown shorts, a peaked green ranger cap with a small yellow star badge, a leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and brown walking boots`.
_deviations.action: The approved prompt wins, and this is why: §8.4 and G5 make an approved asset's prompt+seed its identity, and the approved sprite is the one Hank signed off at a SUPERVISED gate. Substituting the L6 string would generate a different character while claiming to be a regeneration — the exact failure G5 exists to prevent. Every L6 ELEMENT is present (green shirt · ranger cap · star badge · leather satchel · walking boots) and the cape ban is enforced on the negative side, so L6's intent holds; only its 'verbatim' clause does not. `_player.l6Verbatim` keeps the spec string on the record, and tests/unit/manifest.test.ts asserts the elements plus byte-equality with manifest-b0.json's approved row.

_deviations.finding: §9.2 says 'front-load and repeat distinctive anatomy (Fenmaw's gharial snout class of failure)'. The derivation did exactly that and Fenmaw STILL came back a generic crocodile — the subject already read `bulk gharial with a long narrow gharial snout` twice (assets/raw/palette-trials/pt-fenmaw.png). Repetition is not the missing piece: this model reads the SPECIES TERM `gharial` as its common relative `crocodile`, so repeating the term repeats the wrong animal. Confirmed by one generation per hypothesis: replacing the term with the SHAPE — `an extremely long thin tube-shaped snout, a narrow needle-like jaw far longer than the head is wide` — produced a true gharial (pt-fenmaw-b.png). The same collapse is visible in every other trial whose identity rests on a specialist term: `lungfish` rendered a generic bipedal fish blob (pt-mirefin.png), the `wyrm` of `spider-wyrm` vanished and left a plain spider (pt-webvern.png), `spore-antlered` rendered plain deer antlers (pt-sporantle.png), `eyeless` rendered a serpent with large eyes (pt-undermere.png), `will-o-wisp` rendered nothing at all (pt-wispurr.png), `dusk moth` rendered butterfly filaments (pt-gloomoth.png), `mudball tadpole` rendered a bipedal blob with no tail (pt-bogling.png).
_deviations.action: §9.2's fidelity rule gains a second clause, and `_concepts` is where it is applied: NAME DISTINCTIVE ANATOMY BY ITS SHAPE, NEVER BY ITS SPECIES TERM — the term stays (it is the bible's word and G2 protects it), the shape is added beside it and both are then front-loaded and repeated by the derivation. Rewritten: Fenmaw, Mirefin, Webvern, Sporantle, Undermere, Bogling, Wispurr, Gloomoth (each measured above) and Stonewing (reasoned, not measured — no trial exists). Deliberately NOT rewritten: Pyrelisk, because 'basilisk' fixes no anatomy in the bible and a shape restatement would have to invent one. THIS IS A PROMPT CHANGE, NOT A CONTENT CHANGE: every bible name, type, role, habitat and concept term is untouched and still appears verbatim in the subject; only the wording that steers the generator is added. Rewriting what Fenmaw IS would be a G2 violation; describing the gharial's snout by its geometry is a pipeline fidelity fix. Seeds are unaffected — `deriveSeed` is pure in (id, version), so no row's seed moves and G5 is not engaged.

_yearVariantPolicy: build-doc §9.7 caps accepted year variants at 30 and cut line C-2 is 'year variants beyond year 2 for non-slice nodes'. Rows are therefore generated for the four vertical-slice nodes (hearthollow, r1, brackwater, r2) at years 2–6 and for every other node at year 2 only: 4×5 + 8×1 = 28 rows, inside the cap and exactly matching the cut line. Every one of them is img2img (§9.5) and NONE may enter a node JSON without passing tools/overlay-diff (§8.2 / G4).

map-town._skeletonSource: Rewritten after the first full 12-map run (0 PASS / 3 REVISE / 9 REJECT, 121 defects, 39 blocking). REMOVED: 'the buildings are small and compact, none wider than about a twelfth of the picture' — a twelfth of 1024 is 85px and every one of the twelve maps ignored it (hearthollow gym 355x275, brackwater 206x203, bowerdeep 225x220, cindershelf 170x164, duskhollow 146x162). REMOVED: 'with wide open ground between them' — brackwater's reviewer traced the sand plaza to it ('open ground' in a town prompt is a hard dirt/sand-plaza cue) and measured the marsh paved over, centre (512,512) = (233,189,117) sand. ADDED, projection: cindershelf came back a side-on stacked cutaway and r4/r5 flat top-down, so 'chunky three-quarter isometric' alone does not hold — the lit-top-face / two-shaded-side-faces wording is the converging promptFix of the cindershelf, r4 and r5 reviewers, and it is the one statement both failure modes break. ADDED, full bleed: bowerdeep 13.6% pure white + 11.3% water, sanctum 31.1% flat cream. Trial evidence assets/raw/_trials/map-fix-round/: y1-bowerdeep-bleed 0.06% void and terrain on all four edges, y3-cindershelf-bleed-scale 0.02%. ADDED, scale: the path is the ONE element the generator sizes correctly — measured in-band on five maps (r1 track 58-87px, r3 trail 50-85, r5 track 90-110, r2 boardwalk 52, brackwater planking 34) while every building and prop ran 130-355. So the ceiling is anchored to it, and to BOTH axes: height was previously unbounded and is the worse axis (duskhollow cottages 142-162 tall against a 160px screen). ADDED, density (worded as 'the ground between the buildings covered all over with many small things', deliberately NOT 'open ground between them' and deliberately not a request for more BUILDINGS — the first is the cue brackwater's reviewer traced the sand plaza to, the second is the ~50-house grid R1's t1 control produced): object count and object size move together across the six drawn settlements — 4 objects gives 185-355px (hearthollow, cindershelf, bowerdeep), 7 gives 140-206 (duskhollow, brackwater), 9 gives 110-118 (sanctum) — and shrinking objects without raising their number would widen the measured dead zones (brackwater 400x350px of empty plaza, duskhollow 400x450 of empty blue). ADDED, style and hue: 'crisp clean pixel edges' did not hold the idiom — sanctum-approach measured 99.61% functionally grayscale, top eight colours near-duplicate greys, no dark keyline anywhere, lowest edge density of the twelve, and hearthollow / brackwater / r3 / duskhollow each carry a 'not actually pixel art' defect (144k-250k unique colours, anti-aliased edges). The replacement is the converging promptFix of those four reviewers plus the measured absence of the keyline the approved player sprite has. The hue clause is the cohesion pass's sharedDrift measurement: the eight good maps carry 3-7 hue families at >=3% of chromatic pixels, the four bad ones 0-2, and where they collapse the walking surface and the obstacles become the same colour, which is what a 240x160 window cannot read. MAP-PROMPT-RULES R2 (the negative is inert at cfg 1.0) is why every one of these is positive; R4 is why the walkway is a 'lane, track or boardwalk' and never a road.
map-town._gate: UNTRIALLED AGAIN — the first run under this string is SUPERVISED (§9.1 / G13), and the scale clause in particular is the one to measure first. What is trialled: the full-bleed clause (assets/raw/_trials/map-fix-round y1, y3). What is NOT: the path-anchored size ceiling. It rests on measurement (the path lands in-band on five maps, everything else does not) and on three reviewers independently proposing the device (r1, r4, r5 promptFixes), but no cell has run it. Its known failure mode is self-satisfaction — the model can widen the lane instead of shrinking the buildings — so the first check is the RATIO of lane width to building width, not the building width alone. What was tried and FAILED, do not re-ship it: 'drawn from high enough up that a whole house is a small object, about a dozen house-widths across the picture' (map-fix-round y2/y3/y4). Held against y1 at the same seed and subject, it left bowerdeep's houses at 138-166px (y1: 152px) and sanctum's stones at 117x181-197 (shipped: 110-118x188-207) — no movement — and it broke the full-bleed clause standing beside it: y1 0.06% void, y2 29.0% pure white with all four edge rows 100% background, y4 30.0% cream. 'Drawn from high enough up' is a camera-distance request, which is MAP-PROMPT-RULES R5's named failure family.

map-route._skeletonSource: Rewritten after the first full 12-map run. The previous note said routes carry their own scale counter in each node's feature text rather than in the skeleton. Measured: that did not work. All five routes failed scale, and each node's own hedge was ignored — r3's 'closely spaced slender trunks, none of them broad' gave canopy blobs 230-280px with one unbroken 422px run; r5's 'no higher than a person' gave boulders 120-170px wide; r1's 'every one of them small' gave oaks 150x170 and an antler stone 115x205; r4's 'everything on this ground low and small' gave crates at 62-85px and an antler stone 215px tall. A per-node adjective is not a ceiling, so the ceiling moves into the class and is anchored to the one thing every route already gets right: its own path (r1 58-87px, r3 50-85, r5 90-110, r2 52 — all inside or below the 85-140 bar while everything standing on the ground was 2-3x over). Both axes are bound because height is the worse one. The projection clause is here because r4 and r5 came back flat top-down, missing T-17's isometric half outright. The full-bleed clause is shared with map-town and map-site; on a route it is a no-regression addition rather than a fix — assets/raw/_trials/map-fix-round/y5-r4-nobuildings carried it and measured 0.04% void. The style and hue clauses are the class-wide finding no per-node edit can reach: sanctum-approach is a map-route row and it measured 99.61% functionally grayscale with no dark keyline anywhere and the lowest edge density of the twelve. MAP-PROMPT-RULES R2 is why all of it is positive; R4 is why the walkway is a 'path' and never a road; R8 still owns the path's SHAPE, which stays per-node.
map-route._gate: UNTRIALLED — first run SUPERVISED. 'no buildings' is UNCHANGED and is known to be insufficient: r2 drew a cottage and r4 a fortress under it, and the fix trialled for that, y5-r4-nobuildings, FAILED. y5 moved the prohibition to the front of the string ('route map of open wilderness with no buildings of any kind anywhere') and named the specific things ('no houses, no huts, no towers, no walls, only ground and plants and rocks and one path') and the image still came back with a lit-windowed town across the bottom centre. So no new anti-building wording is shipped here — none is evidenced. The r4 reviewer's reading is that the summoner is the word 'town' inside the subject ('drops toward the forge town at the bottom'), which is a _nodes fix and belongs to that pass, not to this class. y5 also still came back flat top-down, which is what the added projection clause is aimed at.

ui-frame._postprocessNote: The one class that SHOULD stretch. A nine-slice frame is meant to be scaled non-uniformly, and letterboxing a square 1024² generation into a 480×96 dialogue box would leave a 96×96 frame floating in the middle of it. Background removal is off for the same reason — after the trim there is no exterior background left, and the 'empty interior' is the panel body, not a hole.

map-site._skeletonSource: Still map-town's skeleton minus every buildings clause and map-route's minus 'no buildings' — a site is a place that is neither a settlement nor a road — and it carries the same four rewrites the other two took after the first 12-map run: projection made concrete (one lit top face, two shaded side faces on a tilted ground plane) because the region's cutaway and flat-top-down failures cross every class; the full-bleed clause, which map-sanctum needs most of the twelve; a size ceiling anchored to the footpath, replacing nothing — the site skeleton never had one, and the stones came back 110-118 wide by 188-207 tall, taller than the whole 160px play window; and the style and hue clauses, which are the class-wide idiom failure the cohesion pass measured. MAP-PROMPT-RULES R2 is why every clause is positive.

hearthollow.feature: a farming hamlet of five buildings set well apart around one open grazing green: Warden Maren's timber field station under a shallow plank roof, a fenced specimen pen and drying racks beside it; a stone-walled gym hall under a steep mossy slate roof, its shed and fenced yard at the foot of the green; a long low inn with a byre; a supply shop with a green awning over its door and an open bait crate outside it; and a deep-thatched cottage between a bare fallow field and standing barley; empty cropped turf with nothing built on it at the exact middle of the picture where a worn dirt lane forks, a tall survey board on a post just below the middle; wildflower meadow and a few oaks on the open ground, one thick hedgerow behind the cottage; the lane climbs out through a timber field gate at the top and goes on to the Meadow Reach
hearthollow.featureSource: ORGANISING IDEA (five buildings standing well apart around one open grazing green, joined by a forking dirt lane) — 'the green' is a shipped place, and the UNCONDITIONAL source is maribel.post.win (when {}) 'Come the turn of the year the whole green goes up in lanterns'. maren.greeting.act1 'Maribel keeps the gym at the bottom of the green' is MAREN's line, not Maribel's (transcription slip in the previous pass, corrected here), and it is CONDITIONAL — when {act:[1], floraStock r1 ≥ 46} — so it is cited for placement only, on top of the unconditional line. festival.hearthollow 'The lanterns are up on the green' is flag-gated on event.festival.open, so it is corroboration, not base state. || ISOMETRIC: this hamlet is separated from the other four towns by ROOF PITCH and WALL MATERIAL, which the isometric view makes load-bearing — shallow plank / steep mossy slate / low byre-ended inn / awning / deep thatch, five different silhouettes at five different heights. Roof and wall materials are art choices in the R7 'concrete structure' class, not named content; the slate and the stone walls are carried from the passing cell assets/raw/_trials/map-town-style/t4-skelA-mapneg. || field station + fenced specimen pen — bible §6 row 1 'Warden Maren's field station'; the pen from maren.opening 'Three in the pen behind you' (act-0 opening cutscene, i.e. the first thing the player sees). Drying racks from the t4 cell. r1.feature: mostly deep grass: wild meadow of long grass, wildflower drifts and tussock, with bramble thickets and low oaks through it, every one of them small. One thin worn dirt track wanders up the picture, swinging wide round each thicket and crossing a shallow stream on planks; at the exact middle of the picture it is worn bare earth with nothing on it; it leaves at the bottom by a gate gap in a broken drystone wall toward the village, and goes on at the top toward the marsh. A granite block taller than a person stands on the north rise above the middle and to its left, branching antlers cut into its face, weather side worn round and pale, turf grown over its foot; a second antler stone, snapped clean off at half its height, stands well below and right of the middle; a wooden forage sign board on a post beside the track just above and left of the middle. No fences, no square fields

brackwater.feature: a stilt town where nothing stands on dry land: five tarred timber buildings on tall piles over open brown water, and one open ferry landing — a fishery shed with nets of different mesh on its rails, an angler's hut with a tally board by its door, a black-tarred gym hall standing highest on the east stilts, an inn whose rooms overhang the water on brackets, a supply shop with bait bundles on a trestle, and at the landing a moored flat-bottomed ferry, a rates post and barrels; crooked plank boardwalks dog-leg between the piles, never straight, meeting on wide empty decking with nothing built on it at the exact middle of the picture; below and left of the middle a stone idol sunk off the dock rim, only the crown of its head showing, face turned out to the channel; the boardwalk reaches stone steps and a low harbour wall at the bottom where a track leaves for the Meadow Reach, and runs on over the water at the top toward the Brackmarsh

r2.feature: mostly dark open water: wide brackish marsh of black shallow water, brown peat banks, reed clumps and half-sunken dead trees, all of them low and small. One narrow weathered plank boardwalk winds the length of the picture in wide shallow S-bends, deep channel water on its left and open shallows on its right, crossing the exact middle of the picture on bare planking with nothing on it, dropping at the bottom onto a mud landing of rotting mooring posts and a leaning jetty toward the stilt town, and reaching firm peat at the top toward the forest. A granite antler stone leans downhill toward the water on a peat bank beside the boardwalk, left of and a little above the middle, peat banked knee high against its uphill side; a squat carved stone figure stands in shallow water right of and below the middle where the reeds thin, turned back to face the town

bowerdeep.feature: a forest town built on one plank walk, all of it flat and all of it at the same height: weathered grey plank decking in deep green shade, curving round each tree and never running straight, the trunks of enormous mossy trees coming straight up through the planking with the boards fitted close around them; standing on the decking, a row of covered night-market stalls under strings of round paper lanterns hung between the trunks overhead, a winding house under a steep shingled roof hung with pale silk skeins, a low oil shed behind it, a gym hall of dark carved wood under deep eaves, and an inn spilling warm orange light from its numbered windows; wide bare planking with nothing built on it at the exact middle of the picture, a market notice board nailed to the handrail just below and right of the middle, papers pinned under it; a long timber stair leads down at the bottom toward the barge landing on the Brackmarsh, and the walk climbs at the top into the Bowerdeep Wilds; the plank decking is the ground here and it covers the entire picture and runs off all four sides, one continuous unbroken surface with no island, no cliff edge, no border and no background showing, drawn from high enough up that a whole house is a small object, about a dozen house-widths across the picture
bowerdeep.featureSource: ORGANISING IDEA — ONE LEVEL, AND THE WALK IS IT. The plank decking is the whole painted ground plane; the forest floor is not painted at all and the trunks pass down through the decking and out of the picture. This REPLACES the previous organising idea (a floor of leaf litter far below plus a walk above it, joined by two stairs) by Hank's ruling of this session, verbatim: "Re-author those two towns at a single level." || WHY — MEASURED. tools/artverify returned REJECT on the first generated bowerdeep map: "a floating diorama island: a square grass-topped plot of earth sitting in open blue water against a pure white sky ... a Minecraft-style vertical dirt cross-section (complete with yellow ore speckles) making up the whole lower half of the picture", with 13.6% of the frame pure white background and ZERO of the two required edge exits present. (That verdict was produced by the review run over the 12 maps and was never written to a file, so it is transcribed here rather than cited to a path.) The full-bleed clause trialled at trials/map-fix-round.json y1/y2 could not overcome it, and that spec's own `question` field records why: the FEATURE ITSELF described vertical levels, and this model renders vertical stacking as a CROSS-SECTION, not as a walkable overhead map. The levels are therefore removed at the source. Isometry stays — T-17 is 'fix scale, keep isometric'. || WORDING: the feature says 'flat' and 'at the same height' and never the word 'level'. The reviewer's own name for the failure was "a platformer LEVEL cross-section", and 'on a single level' in a positive prompt can be read as game-level jargon rather than as flatness; the physical wording cannot. || DIALOGUE RE-CHECKED LINE BY LINE against data/dialogue.json. The walk/floor distinction SURVIVES because the floor and the east stair become referenced places off the painted plane, exactly the way Cindershelf's deep workings already are. amb.bowerdeep-elder.base (when {}): 'Floor stair, was it? They all come up that way. On the walk we would have called that a floor matter, and on the floor they would have sent it up to the walk' + 'I came up to the walk myself the year they re-cut the lower stair' — HOLDS. The town IS the walk, the floor is spoken of and not shown, and the lower stair is the one stair that is still painted: it leads down at the bottom edge. amb.bowerdeep-lampkeeper.base (when {}): 'Pell has the stair. Mine's the walk' and 'First the lower run' — HOLDS on the same footing (two lamp runs, one of them off the painted plane); its 'Oil's in the shed behind the winding house' still lands verbatim, and the oil shed is still painted behind the winding house. amb.bowerdeep-child.base (when {}): 'are you going up the east stair, because I'm not allowed on the east stair' — HOLDS as a reference only; the east stair is deliberately NOT painted (below). Its 'that's my sister up there' is deictic and binds nothing. maren.greeting.bowerdeep (when {}) 'I'm on the forest floor with a glass looking up' and amb.bowerdeep-logger.base (when {}) 'Below the town the Barkhide eat the low growth back to the dirt' — BOTH HOLD, and are in fact easier on a single plane: they describe the floor from off-frame, and neither asks for it in shot. amb.bowerdeep-logger.thin (yearMin 4) 'I've not had a saw out past the east stair in four years' — HOLDS, same referenced-place basis. pell.greeting (when {}) 'Winding house to the stair and back' — HOLDS: both ends of that walk are painted. vendor-bowerdeep.shop (when {}) 'Up on that rail now there's one grazing the moss, and it hasn't noticed there's a stall under it' — HOLDS: the handrail and the stalls are both still on the walk. r3's own feature calls this place 'the canopy town'; a walk among enormous trunks in deep green shade still reads as canopy without the floor under it. || GROUND MATERIAL (R6) MOVED WITH THE LEVEL. 'brown leaf litter and pale root buttresses' lived on the floor and is gone with it; the R6 ground clause is now 'weathered grey plank decking in deep green shade'. The green-shade half of DISTINCTNESS #1's ground-tone lock is kept verbatim, because that was the point of it. || lantern-strung covered night-market stalls — bible §6 row 3 'night market'; prop.bowerdeep-sign-market (when {}) 'NIGHT MARKET — open dusk to dawn. Silk, thread, dye, lamp oil, relight kits'; vendor-bowerdeep.shop (when {}) 'Night market. Dusk to dawn, and no, we don't do mornings'. Lamps and oil are the lampkeeper's trade (amb.bowerdeep-lampkeeper.base, 'mine is two hundred and eleven'), so a lantern-lit walk is base state, not a night variant. || winding house hung with silk skeins — halder.greeting (when {}) 'Silk and thread here, and finished bolt if you want it woven already'; amb.bowerdeep-silkwinder.base (when {}) 'Young stuff comes apart on the frame while you're winding it'; bible §6 row 3 'silk economy off Webvern'. || oil shed behind it — amb.bowerdeep-lampkeeper.base (when {}) 'Oil's in the shed behind the winding house'. || gym hall of dark carved wood — data/gyms.json vesper.town='bowerdeep'; vesper.greeting (when {}) 'Halder pins his order up on the market board. My own figure goes up beside it'. || inn with numbered windows — innkeeper-bowerdeep.rest (when {}) 'The key's on the hook at the stair, second door on the left — seven, eight, nine'. Deliberately NOT given open shutters: shutters are Duskhollow's shipped signature and must not be shared. || DISTINCTNESS #1 — THIS IS THE COLLISION HANK NAMED, and none of it is undone by the single level. Bowerdeep and Duskhollow were both a dark scene lit by many small warm lamps, both a ribbon of buildings along one linear element, and both ended their prop clause with the identical six words 'notice board on a post at its ___'. The three separations still stand, with the opposite of each still written into Duskhollow: (1) FIXTURE — round paper lanterns strung BETWEEN THE TRUNKS OVERHEAD, against Duskhollow's tall iron lamp posts standing on the ground. (2) COLOUR TEMPERATURE — warm orange light, against Duskhollow's pale cold lamps and cold blue half-light. (3) GROUND TONE — 'deep green shade' plus, now, 'weathered grey plank decking' in place of the leaf litter; the tone lock survives the level change, and grey plank against Duskhollow's 'thin grey-green turf, bare rock and heather' is a wider separation than the litter was. The shared prop sentence is still gone: this board is NAILED TO A HANDRAIL, not on a post. || PROP PLACEMENT — bowerdeep-sign-market (sign-card, x520 y560 in data/nodes/bowerdeep.json) is 8 px right of centre and 48 px BELOW it, i.e. 'just below and right of the middle'; re-checked against the node file this pass. Props have no sprite, so it must BE in the painting. The HANDRAIL is shipped: vendor-bowerdeep.shop (when {}) 'Up on that rail now ... there's a stall under it.' The loose papers are prop.bowerdeep-sign-market (when {}) 'Pinned under it on a scrap: the Webvern figure, midsummer.' || CENTRE: 'wide bare planking with nothing built on it at the exact middle of the picture' — native (512,512) is open deck, and the notice board at 520/560 is off the spawn tile. || EXITS: adjacency ['r2','r3']. BOTTOM a long timber stair leads down toward the barge landing on the Brackmarsh (r2, back toward Hearthollow) — one structure doing two jobs, the shipped 'lower stair' of amb.bowerdeep-elder.base and the bottom edge exit at once. The barge is halder.quest.silk.done (when flagged) 'Bolt goes out on the morning barge', corroborated unconditionally by wick.greeting.town (when {}) 'A barge three days late'. TOP the walk itself climbs on into the Bowerdeep Wilds (r3). No other edge described (R3). || FULL-BLEED + SCALE CLAUSES carried from trials/map-fix-round.json y1/y2. The full-bleed wording is adapted by two words — 'one continuous unbroken SURFACE' where the trial said 'a continuous piece of TERRAIN' — because on this node the ground IS decking and calling it terrain would fight the clause it is in. The scale comparative is verbatim. Note the one deliberate tension left in: the bottom stair leads DOWN while the same sentence asks for 'no cliff edge'. A stair head in the decking is the licensed exception — it is the edge exit, it is the shipped lower stair, and it is the only place in the picture where anything leaves the plane. If the next generation turns that stair back into a cross-section, the stair is what to cut, not the exit. || SCALE: no 'small and compact' clause — the map-town skeleton carries it. || NOT PAINTED, so the next pass does not think it was missed: (a) the forest floor, and with it the leaf litter and the pale root buttresses — removed by the ruling, and the direct cause of the reject; (b) the east stair (amb.bowerdeep-child.base) — a second stair leaving the plane is the failure mode being repaired, and there are only two edge exits to spend; (c) the barge landing itself, which is now beyond the bottom edge at the foot of the stair rather than in shot; (d) the council side of the market (halder.quest.silk.deferred) — it was not painted before this pass either. || OPEN, NOT RESOLVED (unchanged by this pass): bible §6 row 3 calls the market a 'night market (Dark spawns while shopping)' and the shipped dialogue is emphatic it is dusk-to-dawn only, but each node ships ONE base map plus (currently empty) yearVariants. Lit lanterns are written in without forcing a night palette. Whether Bowerdeep's base map should be painted at night is a decision nobody has made.

r3.feature: mostly dark forest floor: deep wild woodland of moss, ferns, deadfall and mushroom clumps under closely spaced slender trunks, none of them broad, in heavy green shade. One narrow trodden trail threads from the foot of the picture to the top, doubling back on itself twice where the ground steepens, running down toward the canopy town at the bottom and climbing onto bare stony ground at the top toward the ash country. A small felled clearing lies well above and right of the middle, its fresh stumps and one stack of cut logs set back off the trail, painted blaze marks on the trunks standing around it; at the exact middle of the picture the trail is bare trodden dirt with nothing on it. Above and left of the middle a granite stone stands wedged between two trunks gone flat where they press against its sides, its face cut into branching antlers
r3.featureSource: FORM is the w4/w6 winner: terrain lead, enumeration, then the trail as thin and secondary. 'deep wild woodland' = data/nodes/r3.json biome Forest + bible §6 routes 'R3 Bowerdeep Wilds'. moss, ferns, deadfall and mushroom clumps are ground cover, not named content. || SCALE COUNTER: 'closely spaced slender trunks, none of them broad' — aimed straight at the measured defect (w5/w6 drew canopies at ~200-230 native px, a full screen per tree); a forest map is where that failure is worst. Wording is unlike the other five routes'. || PATH SHAPE, unique to this route: 'threads up … doubling back on itself twice where the ground steepens'. Not the 'meanders … curving round' sentence the previous pass repeated on five of six routes. || ISOMETRIC: the doubling-back and 'where the ground steepens' give this view relief to render; the change to bare stony ground at the top is a grade change, which reads far better isometrically than flat. || felled clearing, stumps, log stack, blaze marks — amb.r3-logger.base (when {}) 'We cut marked stands and nothing else. The marks come down from the town' and 'Webvern in the tops over this stand, so we cut round those trees' (which is why standing trunks remain round the clearing); bible §6 row 3 'Cullbrand logging subplot'; wick.act3.loss 'a clause in the wilds contract … puts a Company man on a marked stand' (actMin 3, corroboration only). Stumps, log stacks and blazes are R7's reliably-landing structure class. || CENTRE FIXED — this was a real contract FAILURE in the previous pass, which put the clearing 'beside the trail at the middle' and defended it with 'a clearing is open ground either way'. It is not: fresh stumps and a stack of cut logs are solid, and chooseSpawnTile → firstWalkableTile searches outward from (512,512). The clearing is now moved 'well above and right of the middle' with its stumps and logs 'set back off the trail', and the centre is stated positively and separately: 'the trail at the exact middle of the picture is bare trodden dirt with nothing on it'. || PROP — r3-antler-canopy (antler-stone, x430 y336 = 82 px left of centre, 176 px above it) is 'above and left of the middle'. Its detail is prop.r3-antler-canopy verbatim-in-substance: 'Two trunks stand hard against its sides, and both trunks have gone flat where they touch it.' That is this stone's own shipped uniqueness, replacing the nine repeated words the previous pass used on all six routes. || EXITS: adjacency ['bowerdeep','cindershelf']. BOTTOM 'toward the canopy town' = Bowerdeep (bible §6 row 3 'Forest canopy'). TOP 'onto bare stony ground toward the ash country' = Cindershelf's Volcanic steppe (bible §6 row 4); the trees thinning to bare stone is the biome hand-off and the visible top-end marker, and it keeps R3 — it says where the trail goes, not what the edge holds.

cindershelf.feature: a mining town on one flat open ash yard, every building standing on the same ground at the same height, ore-cart rails laid flat across the ash between them: a relic forge with a tall smoking chimney and a glowing forge mouth, a small squat gym forge of dark basalt block a short way off across the ash with a black slag heap between the two, an inn with steaming stone bathing tubs outside it, a supply shop under a soot-stained awning, and a boarded-up company store beside it, windows nailed over; left of the middle a timbered shaft head with winch and ore carts over a dark shaft mouth, and beside it, level with the middle, a low shrine of curved fired plates fitted without mortar, candles burnt into hollows along the joins; lower and right of the middle a second timbered ladder head down into the deep workings; black volcanic ash, cracked basalt, steam vents and glowing orange fissures and no grass anywhere; bare flat ash with nothing built on it at the exact middle of the picture between the shaft head and the forge; a cinder track leaves at the bottom for the Bowerdeep Wilds, stone stairs climb out at the top onto the Cinder Steppe; the ground covers the entire picture and runs off all four sides, a continuous piece of terrain with no island, no cliff edge, no border and no background showing, drawn from high enough up that a whole house is a small object, about a dozen house-widths across the picture
cindershelf.featureSource: ORGANISING IDEA — ONE LEVEL: a single flat ash yard, everything standing on the same ground, joined by ore-cart rails laid flat across it. This REPLACES 'five buildings on cut basalt benches at different heights down one ash scarp, joined by stone stairs' by Hank's ruling of this session, verbatim: "Re-author those two towns at a single level." The scarp is gone from the painting altogether — not moved to an edge, because an edge is R3's forbidden subject and a cliff at one is the thing the full-bleed clause in this same string forbids. || WHY — MEASURED. tools/artverify returned REJECT on the first generated cindershelf map: it came back as "a SIDE-ON MINE CUTAWAY: three horizontal shelves stacked one above the other in the picture plane, every building drawn in flat front elevation ... There is no ground plane anywhere in the image — not one surface recedes, no roof shows two faces, no terrace shows its floor", which the reviewer called "a platformer level cross-section, not Cindershelf". (That verdict came from the review run over the 12 maps and was never written to a file, so it is transcribed here rather than cited to a path.) The full-bleed clause trialled at trials/map-fix-round.json y3 could not overcome it, and that spec's own `question` field records why: the FEATURE ITSELF described vertical levels, and this model renders vertical stacking as a cross-section rather than as a walkable overhead map. Isometry stays — T-17 is 'fix scale, keep isometric'; it is the stacking that goes. || WORDING: the feature says 'flat' and 'at the same height' and never the word 'level'. The reviewer's own name for the failure was "a platformer LEVEL cross-section", and 'on a single level' in a positive prompt can be read as game-level jargon rather than as flatness; the physical wording cannot. || DIALOGUE RE-CHECKED LINE BY LINE against data/dialogue.json, and the shipped lines are POSITIVELY BETTER on one plane than on a staircase of benches. sable.post.loss (when {}), the line the two forges are separated by, reads in full: 'Bench is still warm. I'm not banking it down yet. My forge is the small one, thirty feet that way. Give the door a good bang. A soft knock won't carry.' — HOLDS, and it is the primary evidence for the single plane: 'thirty feet THAT WAY' is horizontal, and the two forges are separated by SIZE (tall relic forge with a smoking chimney against the small squat gym forge), which is what the line itself does. The painted distance between them is 'a short way off across the ash' rather than a figure in feet, because a number in a prompt renders as a number. amb.cindershelf-shafthand.base (when {}): 'A vent opens and the ground round it goes soft. Soft ground is what we cut, so the housing went up BEHIND the shaft, which is why the whole east row leans' — HOLDS: behind is horizontal and leaning is not stacking; nothing here asks for terraces. Its 'The shrines. We didn't put them there and we don't move them' is plural and remains the grounding for two shrine hotspots. greaves.act4.steppe (actMin 4): 'There are men on this STREET who ate better under that contract' — HOLDS, and a street is a single plane. amb.cindershelf-worker.base (when {}): 'My wife was born three doors up from where we live now' — HOLDS, horizontal. bram.warm.1 (actMin 4) 'The men underground call it the warm shell below. GO UP and look at the shrine at the shaft head' and bram.warm.2 'You got UP to the shrine, then' — CHECKED, and they HOLD as idiom: 'go up' is 'go up the yard', and the only vertical the shipped lines actually require is DOWN into the workings, which IS painted, twice, as the shaft mouth and the ladder head. A low rise under the shaft head was drafted to make 'up' literal and then cut deliberately: the shrine prop sits at the shaft head at native (372,508) and the player has to stand within 48 px of it, so raising that ground risks painting the hotspot onto a tile the collision mask will not make walkable — a mechanical cost against a piece of idiom. sable.greeting (when {}) 'Colder up there than down here' — CHECKED, non-binding: 'up there' is the Cinder Steppe (r4), which is off this map at the top exit, exactly as maren.greeting.act4's 'Nine months since I was up there myself' uses it. bram.greeting (when {}) 'Mind your feet that side. Hot scale down there and it goes through a boot sole' — HOLDS: 'down there' is the floor at his own feet. gerta.greeting (when {}) 'off the wall of the third shaft' and amb.cindershelf-miner.base (when {}) 'before I'm off the second ladder' — HOLD: the deep workings were already off the painted plane and still are. || GROUND — carried verbatim from the R6-measured winner (palette-trials/pt-map-cindershelf vs round3/v2-cindershelf): black volcanic ash, cracked basalt, steam vents, glowing orange fissures, no grass anywhere. This clause turned two-volcanoes-on-a-lawn into basalt and ash and is the one clause that must never be cut for length. R4's banned word stays absent: the ways out are a cinder track and stone stairs, never the word the grey ring road at round3/v2-cindershelf came from. || relic forge — bible §6 row 4 'relic forge (retirement relics crafted here)'; bram.greeting (when {}) 'The bellows are on your left'; bible §9 'Forge a Legacy'. || gym forge — data/gyms.json sable.town='cindershelf'; sable.post.loss (when {}) as quoted above. || slag heap — NEW this pass and shipped, not invented: sable.post.win (when {}) 'Bram's through the back, past the slag heap.' It earns its place twice over — it is an R7 concrete non-building structure, and it is the shipped line that puts the two forges apart HORIZONTALLY, which is the work the removed benches used to do. || inn with steaming stone bathing tubs — innkeeper-cindershelf.rest (when {}) 'There's a tub going now, and the tubs fill straight off the hot spring'. || supply shop under a soot-stained awning, and the boarded-up company store next to it — vendor-cindershelf.shop (when {}) 'My prices went up the month next door boarded its windows'. That line is UNCONDITIONAL and is the primary source; greaves.act4.steppe 'the company store shut in the week the crew were paid off' is actMin 4 + flag and is corroboration only. This is the shipped read of bible §6 row 4 'arrival mid-collapse'. || SHAFT. The unconditional grounding is gerta.greeting (when {}) 'One reading a shift, off the wall of the third shaft, thirty-one years of it' and amb.cindershelf-shafthand.base (when {}), which also ships 'Nobody has got round to the loose bit down by the winch' — the winch. bram.mine.expanding and bram.mine.closing stay dropped: their whens are {yearMin 5, r4 cragmar-line >= 12} and {yearMin 5, <= 3}, mutually exclusive year-variant states, neither true in the base year this map paints. 'over a dark adit' is now 'over a dark shaft mouth': a winch and a headframe stand over a VERTICAL shaft, which is what every shipped line describes ('Six days in seven I'm down it', 'below the shaft', 'got down to the deep shrine'), and an adit is a horizontal drift that has to be cut into a rock face — i.e. it was quietly asking for the scarp back. || CENTRE: 'bare flat ash with nothing built on it at the exact middle of the picture between the shaft head and the forge', with the shaft head anchored left of the middle so the open ground has two named sides. Native (512,512) is where the player spawns on every arrival. || PROP PLACEMENT, re-checked against data/nodes/cindershelf.json this pass — props have no sprite, so each must BE in the painting. cindershelf-shrine-mine (shell-kiln-shrine, x372 y508) is 140 px left of centre and 4 px above it, i.e. 'beside it, level with the middle'; its detail is prop.cindershelf-shrine-mine verbatim-in-substance: 'A low structure at the shaft head, built of curved plates fitted without mortar' and 'Candles have been set along the joins, and they have worn hollows into the plate underneath.' || cindershelf-shrine-deep (x706 y604 = 194 px right of centre, 92 px below it) CANNOT BE PAINTED AS ITSELF: prop.cindershelf-shrine-deep puts it 'at the bottom of the deep workings, past the last ladder', where 'the air is still and a candle flame stands straight up', and it is a different object from the shaft-head shrine (a single plate with no joins, KILNBACK cut across the face). MAP-PROMPT-RULES sanctions the remedy: 'the prop's x/y is moved afterwards to wherever the painting put it'. So the painting puts a second timbered LADDER HEAD at 706/604 and the hotspot stays on it — the player interacts at the ladder head and the shipped text narrates the descent. Ladders are shipped: amb.cindershelf-miner.base (when {}) 'Hands know it before I'm off the second ladder', and bram.warm.3 (actMin 4 + kilnback flags) 'Mind the last ladder, third rung's split.' || EXITS: adjacency ['r3','r4']. BOTTOM a cinder track for the Bowerdeep Wilds (r3, back toward Hearthollow). TOP stone stairs climb onto the Cinder Steppe (r4, on toward the Sanctum) — kept word for word from the shipped string, because it is the one exit that has to read as a climb (the art convention has the Sanctum at the top because you climb to it) and both words are R4-safe. Destinations only (R3). || FULL-BLEED + SCALE CLAUSES carried verbatim from trials/map-fix-round.json y3. They were not enough on their own; they are kept because the failure they target (13.6% white background and a cross-section) is the failure this node produced, and the cause they could not overcome — the feature naming levels — is what this rewrite removes. || SCALE: no 'small and compact' clause — the map-town skeleton carries it. || NOT PAINTED, so the next pass does not think it was missed: (a) the ash scarp and every cut basalt bench — removed by the ruling, and the direct cause of the reject; (b) the low ash rise under the shaft head, cut for the collision reason given above; (c) the leaning east row of miners' housing (amb.cindershelf-shafthand.base) — a row of houses is exactly the filler Hank objected to, and the skeleton's building budget is spent; (d) Bram's warm flagstone (bram.warm.1/.3), which is inside the relic forge and not on the map at all.
cindershelf.agingArc: vents flare, mine expands or closes

r4.feature: mostly black ash: open volcanic steppe of black ash flats and cracked basalt, steaming vents, thin glowing orange fissures, loose cinder blocks and dry ash-grey scrub tufts, everything on this ground low and small, and no green grass anywhere. One thin ash path runs almost straight up the picture, jinking only where it steps round a vent, a disused narrow rail line, coiled cable and open wooden crates left along it and one heavy abandoned rail lying near the top; the path crosses the exact middle of the picture on packed ash with nothing on it, drops toward the forge town at the bottom, and climbs a low basalt scarp at the top toward the dark vale. Above and right of the middle a granite antler stone stands beside a steaming vent, windward face glazed to a skin of crazed lifting glass, sheltered face cut sharp
r4.featureSource: GROUND — 'black ash flats and cracked basalt … no green grass anywhere' is R6 applied verbatim in spirit: the exact clause that turned Cindershelf's two-volcanoes-on-a-lawn into basalt, ash, steam vents and orange fissures (palette-trials/pt-map-cindershelf vs round3/v2-cindershelf). Biome = data/nodes/r4.json Steppe + bible §6 routes 'R4 Cinder Steppe'. 'ash path' is one of R4's approved substitutes for the banned word. || SCALE COUNTER: 'everything on this ground low and small' — phrased for a treeless biome where the offenders are cinder blocks and scrub tufts rather than trees. Unlike the other five routes' wording. || PATH SHAPE, unique to this route: 'runs almost straight up the picture … jinking only where it steps round a vent'. This is the one route whose path is nearly straight, and it is earned rather than lazy — amb.r4-worker.base (when {}) says 'You can follow the cable runs the whole way up from the vent line', a single continuous run up the scarp. It is deliberately the opposite of r3's doubling-back and r5's kinking. || ISOMETRIC: a low basalt scarp at the top, steaming vents standing proud of the flats, and a rail line running up a grade are all relief; the scarp is the top-end marker and is dialogue-sourced. || INDUSTRIAL LEAVINGS, all from amb.r4-worker.base, which is UNCONDITIONAL (when {}): 'The lid's off that crate — they come open on their own'; 'Contract's shut, so I'm pulling cable and rail out'; 'There's a rail up top that four of us couldn't shift. It's still up there.' The 'up top' is why the heavy rail is placed near the top of the picture. Rails and crates are R7's reliably-landing structure class. || 'low basalt scarp' — amb.r4-worker.base's ground, and amb.cindershelf-worker.base (when {}) 'West scarp crew'. || THE ECOLOGICAL AFTERMATH IS NOT PAINTED, on purpose. Bible §6 says "Cindershelf's 'arrival mid-collapse' is produced, never baked", the act-4 raid fires on entry, and G6 forbids scripting it — so no empty nest, no thinned ground, no carrion. amb.r4-worker.emptied's 'The nest on the west scarp is empty … the white streak underneath has gone grey' is population-gated (stonewing-line ≤ 1) and is deliberately not used. || CONFLICT RECORDED, not resolved: amb.r4-worker.arrival (actMin 4, flagsUnset story.steppe.arrival.seen) names 'There's a kettle on at the hut' — a hut on R4. The map-route skeleton says no buildings, so no hut is painted; the line stays true only if the hut is off-frame. || PROP — r4-antler-vent (antler-stone, x596 y288 = 84 px right of centre, 224 px above it) is 'above and right of the middle'. Its detail is prop.r4-antler-vent verbatim-in-substance: 'Vent heat has glazed the windward face of this stone to a skin of glass, and the glass has crazed and lifted in patches … The sheltered face has none of that, and the cutting there is sharp.' || CENTRE: 'the path crosses the exact middle of the picture on packed ash with nothing on it' — every vent, fissure and cinder block is stepped round rather than placed on it, and the stone is anchored above and right. || EXITS: adjacency ['cindershelf','duskhollow']. BOTTOM 'toward the forge town' = Cindershelf (bible §6 row 4 'relic forge'). TOP 'climbs a low basalt scarp … toward the dark vale' = Duskhollow (bible §6 row 5 'Dusk vale').

duskhollow.feature: five buildings strung out in a loose line along one dirt track lit by tall iron lamp posts evenly spaced on the ground beside it, every shutter open: a domed stone observatory alone on a bare knoll above the track, a torn notice board on a post at the foot of its steps just above the middle, an inn with one pale lamp burning in each open window, a lampwright's workshop with oil jars stacked outside and lamp frames on a bench, a supply shop, and a gym hall sunk into the slope below the track behind steps going down into the dark; a shepherd's fold of dry-stone walling, thin grey-green turf, bare rock and heather, all in cold blue half-light; open turf with nothing built on it at the exact middle of the picture beside the track; the track runs down at the bottom toward the Cinder Steppe and climbs past the last lamp post at the top into Duskhollow Vale
duskhollow.featureSource: ORGANISING IDEA (a ribbon of buildings strung along one lamplit track on a vale floor, every shutter open, the observatory alone above and the gym sunk below) — bible §6 row 5 'Dusk vale … observatory'; the observatory dome from tools/comfy/manifest.json _nodes.duskhollow 'a dusk vale town under an observatory dome'. The lamp line is shipped: amb.duskhollow-lampwright.base (when {}) 'The wick gauge matters more than the oil does, and mine is fourteen to the inch'; vendor-duskhollow.shop (when {}) 'The observatory buys its oil off the lampwright direct and walks past this door to do it' — which also puts the lampwright and the shop on the same line with the observatory apart from both. || CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS PASS'S OWN CLAIM: it asserted 'No other node of mine uses a linear/ribbon plan.' That is FALSE — Bowerdeep also strings its structures along one linear element (the plank walk). The two are therefore separated by LEVEL, PALETTE and LIGHT SOURCE rather than by plan: Bowerdeep is warm orange light and round paper lanterns hung overhead between trunks in green canopy shade on an elevated walk; Duskhollow is cold pale lamps in tall iron posts standing on the ground of a bare vale floor. Fixture, height, colour temperature and ground tone are all opposite, deliberately. The shared six-word prop ending is gone too — Bowerdeep's board is nailed to a handrail, this one is torn on a post. || ISOMETRIC: this town's whole shape is a HEIGHT story, which is why it survives the new view best — the domed observatory stands alone up on a knoll ABOVE the track, the gym hall is sunk BELOW it behind steps going down, and the five buildings sit on the vale floor between them. Three levels, one line. || every shutter standing open — innkeeper-duskhollow.rest (when {}) 'Shutters stay open. Top and bottom, all night, every room. Rule eleven, and the observatory wrote it, not me'; amb.duskhollow-child.base (when {}) 'My shutters are open all night and my lamp's out'. (maren.act5.duskhollow 'The houses keep their shutters open all night for the observatory' is actMin 5 + flag — corroboration only.) Shutters are Duskhollow's alone; no other town in this pass is given them. || observatory alone on a knoll above the track — bible §6 row 5 'observatory'; the height is shipped in innkeeper-duskhollow.rest (when {}) 'That argument lives up the hill, and I'd walk it if I were you'. ives.greeting (when {}) 'Two censuses in this building' and 'the standard is nailed up beside the door'; orrin.greeting (when {}) 'Through the arch on the left, and mind the step.' || PROP PLACEMENT — duskhollow-sign-observatory (sign-card, x500 y430) is 12 px left of centre and 82 px ABOVE it, so 'at the foot of its steps just above the middle' lands it. 'Torn' is prop.duskhollow-sign-observatory (when {}) verbatim: 'Most of this board is torn at the tacks.' Its text 'PLATES THIS YEAR and then the figure nine' and 'shelf hours on the door' back the census board; bible §9 'The Star Census'. || inn with one pale lamp per open window — innkeeper-duskhollow.rest as above; the single-lamp count is the deliberate opposite of Bowerdeep's strings of lanterns and is corroborated by amb.duskhollow-elder.base (when {}) 'Same three rooms, same two lamps.' || lampwright's workshop, oil jars, lamp frames on a bench — amb.duskhollow-lampwright.base (when {}) 'Cold-pressed, then strained through flannel, then strained again' and the wick-gauge line; amb.duskhollow-elder.base (when {}) 'I am buying oil now at a rate I never used to … there was a wick in my hand when you came through that door, because I trim my own.' || supply shop — speaker vendor-duskhollow (Hesk), vendor-duskhollow.shop (when {}) 'Not that tin, that's for the wick. Fill's in the flat tin at the end.' || gym hall SUNK BELOW THE TRACK behind steps going down into a dark doorway — data/gyms.json noct.town='duskhollow'; noct.pre 'Room's dark. It stays dark. Bring a lamp for the walk down' (gated only on the gym not yet being beaten, i.e. base state) and noct.post.loss (when {}) 'The door's not locked. It is the same dark at noon.' || shepherd's fold — amb.duskhollow-shepherd.base (when {}) 'The ground's thin up the vale and dark half the day. The flock does very well on it.' The FOLD itself is an inference from the flock, drawn as dry-stone walling; it is a structure and a material, not named content, and is recorded here as inferred rather than quoted. || thin grey-green turf, bare rock, heather, cold blue half-light — data/nodes/duskhollow.json biome Vale; noct.greeting (when {}) 'Dark at four here in winter. Under the rim it goes earlier still'; amb.duskhollow-shepherd.base's 'ground's thin'. || CENTRE: 'open turf at the exact middle of the picture beside the track, with nothing built on it'. Everything solid is deliberately off-centre — the observatory is up on its knoll, the gym is sunk into the slope, the five buildings are strung along the line. || EXITS: adjacency ['r4','r5']. r5.feature: mostly dark turf: narrow vale floor of dark blue-green cropped grass, dead bracken and low heather under cold blue twilight, pale lichen-blotched boulders no higher than a person, scree fans off the valley sides, no bright green anywhere, and one still black pool lying against the foot of the left-hand valley side well away from the middle. One thin pale sheep track climbs the whole way up the picture, kinking round each boulder in short straight runs rather than smooth curves, passing over the exact middle of the picture on bare pale earth with nothing on it, dropping down the vale at the bottom toward the observatory town and climbing out of the vale head at the top onto bare grey rising ground toward the mountain. Below and left of the middle one granite antler stone stands quite alone, nothing but grass around it for a long way, its carving worn shallow the whole way round
r5.featureSource: 'vale floor / dusk' = data/nodes/r5.json biome Vale + bible §6 routes 'R5 Duskhollow Vale' and §6 row 5 'Dusk vale'. 'cold blue twilight … no bright green anywhere' is R6 applied to a dusk biome — naming the ground colour is the only measured way to stop the model defaulting to a lawn. The darkness has a shipped rate: amb.r5-astronomer.base (when {}) 'The vale goes dark at about a degree a decade.' || ONE STONE, NOT MANY. tools/comfy/manifest.json _nodes.r5.feature says 'a shadowed vale of standing stones' — plural, and unsourced. Bible §6 gives r5 only the row name, data/nodes/r5.json ships exactly ONE antler stone, and prop.r5-antler-vale says 'nothing higher than the grass for a quarter mile in any direction'. One stone and natural boulders are painted. || SCALE COUNTER: 'boulders no higher than a person' — an absolute height rather than the 'many small … none of them large' formula, and unlike the other five routes' wording. || PATH SHAPE, unique to this route: 'a sheep track … kinking round each boulder in short straight runs rather than smooth curves'. This is the deliberate break of the sentence r5 previously shared verbatim with r1, r2 and r3 ('meanders across the whole picture from bottom to top through the middle, curving round the X'). A sheep track is also a different KIND of path from every other route's, which is the point. || DISTINCTNESS FROM r1 — the previous pass shared 16 five-grams between these two: same lead shape, same enumeration shape, same path sentence, same nine-word stone, separated only by palette. This pass changes the path verb, the path geometry, the scale-counter form, the stone's description and the relief (r1 has a rise, r5 has valley sides on both hands with scree coming off them). || ISOMETRIC: valley sides rising on both hands, scree fans coming off them and a vale head to climb out of are exactly the relief this view renders; the previous flat reading wasted all of it. || POOL ANCHORED — contract FAILURE in the previous pass, which left 'a still black pool' in the enumeration with no position and admitted as much ('The still black pool is unplaced'). MAP-PROMPT-RULES names a lake as one of the three things with a direct mechanical consequence when painted dead centre. It is now 'lying against the foot of the left-hand valley side, well away from the middle'. || CENTRE: 'passing over the exact middle on bare pale earth with nothing on it', stated positively on the sanctum-approach model. || PROP — r5-antler-vale (antler-stone, x344 y618 = 168 px left of centre, 106 px below it) is 'below and left of the middle'. Both of its painted details are prop.r5-antler-vale's own: 'It stands in open ground, with nothing higher than the grass for a quarter mile in any direction' and 'The cutting is shallow the whole way round.' No other stone in the region is described this way. || EXITS: adjacency ['duskhollow','sanctum-approach']. BOTTOM 'down the vale … toward the observatory town' = Duskhollow (bible §6 row 5 'observatory; star census'). TOP 'climbing out of the vale head … onto bare grey rising ground toward the mountain' = the Sanctum Approach, which the edge convention puts at the top because you climb to it; it is named as TERRAIN rather than as the Sanctum so this frame does not try to paint the caldera itself.

sanctum-approach.feature: mostly grey ash and bare rock: one long ascent up the flank of a crater, drifted grey ash over cracked stone, low cut-rock retaining walls, scree fans and fallen blocks, none of them bigger than a crate, no plants anywhere. A single wide stone stair climbs the whole height of the picture in long switchbacks, crossing an open level landing of bare ash at the exact middle, reaching a dark cleft cut in the crater wall at the top and dropping away at the bottom toward the vale. Beside the stair low down, on the centre line well below the middle, a tall granite stone set into cut rock rather than into ground, branching antlers above a walking herd cut across its outward face; beside the stair much higher up, above the middle on the same line, a second unfinished stone, antlers roughed out to half their depth, a hammer and three wedges at its foot half buried in ash
sanctum-approach.featureSource: 'one long ascent' = bible §6 row 6 verbatim-in-substance, 'no shops, one long approach', and MAP-PROMPT-RULES' note that the Sanctum sits at the top because you climb to it. 'stone stair … in long switchbacks' is R4-approved vocabulary, and the SHAPE is named rather than the endpoints because R8 measured that endpoint-only paths render dead straight. || R4 HYGIENE — both of this node's prop dialogue entries use R4's banned word for the way up (prop.sanctum-approach-antler-gate and prop.sanctum-approach-antler-inner each contain it). It is genuinely in the shipped dialogue, so this is not a G2 problem, but the banned word must not sit in the prompt file, where a grep-based gate would trip on it and where it could be pasted into a subject by accident. The quotes are therefore TRIMMED to the part actually being used: prop.sanctum-approach-antler-gate '… about double the height of the one out in the vale' (which is why this stone is 'tall' and not merely 'large') and 'This stone carries the herd on both faces, and none of the others does'; prop.sanctum-approach-antler-inner 'The antlers are roughed out to about half their depth'. || ISOMETRIC: a switchback stair climbing the FLANK of a crater is a pure height composition, and the two stones now read at different elevations on it rather than as two objects on a flat plane. || 'crater / crater wall' = bible §6 row 6 'Sealed caldera'. 'drifted grey ash' = prop.sanctum-approach-antler-inner (when {}) 'The ash over them takes a boot in to the ankle, and none of it is broken.' 'no plants anywhere' = data/nodes/sanctum-approach.json floraStock 35 with only carricrow-line present, and maren.greeting.sanctum-approach (when {}) 'The only thing living on this approach is crows, and crows are what I'm counting.' || SCALE COUNTER: 'fallen blocks, none of them bigger than a crate' — a concrete comparison object rather than the repeated 'none of them large' formula, and unlike the other five routes' wording. || PROPS — PLACEMENT AMBIGUITY FIXED. Both stones sit on the centre line in the data (x=512) but 388 native px apart vertically, and the previous string said the second one 'stands beside it higher up', where 'it' read as the gate stone. sanctum-approach-antler-gate (antler-stone, x512 y760 = on the centre line, 248 px BELOW centre) is now 'beside the stair low down on the centre line well below the middle'; sanctum-approach-antler-inner (x512 y372 = on the centre line, 140 px ABOVE centre) is 'beside the stair much higher up, above the middle on the same line'. Both are beside the STAIR, not beside each other. || DISTINCTNESS #4 — each stone now carries its own shipped uniqueness instead of the nine words the previous pass used on all six routes. The gate stone: prop.sanctum-approach-antler-gate 'This stone carries the herd on both faces, and none of the others does' and 'On the outward face the six are walking in' → 'a walking herd cut across its outward face'. The inner stone: prop.sanctum-approach-antler-inner (when {} — unconditional) 'The antlers are roughed out to about half their depth' and 'Tools lie at the foot of it under the ash: a hammer and three wedges, side by side. The ash over them takes a boot in to the ankle.' The tools are restored here because they are shipped, unconditional, and they are what makes this stone unlike every other stone in the region. || CENTRE: 'crossing an open level landing of bare ash at the exact middle' — this is the strongest of the twelve and is the wording the other eleven were brought up to. The landing between the two stones is what the player spawns onto at native (512,512). || EXITS: adjacency ['r5','sanctum']. BOTTOM the stair 'drops away … toward the vale' = r5, Duskhollow Vale, back down the chain. TOP 'a dark cleft cut in the crater wall' = the Sanctum, painted as an opening in rock rather than as architecture. This is the only node whose top exit is a hole in rock rather than a change of terrain, which is correct for a sealed caldera. || CONFLICTS RECORDED, not resolved: (1) wick.act6.pre names 'a thing up on rollers past the gate stone … rated to carry the weight of a barge' — an act-6 story object, not in the base map. (2) The gate's OPEN/SHUT state changes in the fiction (maren.greeting.act6 'The gate is standing open. It has not been open in my lifetime'), while amb.sanctum-approach-scout.base (when {}) says 'That gate was already open when we got here'. This node paints an undifferentiated dark cleft and commits to neither; an open/shut distinction, if wanted, is a year/act variant, not this pass.

sanctum.feature: mostly short grazed grass and pale volcanic grit: a ring of nine tall grey standing stones at the middle of the picture, evenly spaced, every one facing in toward the centre, each carved with a single antlered stag on its own, cut deep and large on the face; inside the ring the grass is grazed short and even, and the exact middle of the picture is open grazed grass with nothing standing on it, while outside the ring the grass stands knee high everywhere; fallen slabs, dry heather and a few dead trees on the wide flat floor around it; one worn footpath climbs in at the bottom through a tall gate standing open in a face of cut dark rock, comes up to the ring and enters it through a gap between two stones
sanctum.featureSource: CLASS CHANGE IS THE REAL FIX — tools/comfy/manifest.json _nodes.sanctum.kind is 'town', so this string previously composed into the map-town skeleton, which mandates buildings with doors. The Sanctum has none (bible §6 row 6: 'Sealed caldera | league + finale; no shops, one long approach'), and nothing in bible §6/§7/§9/§10/§11 or data/dialogue.json names a building, hall or structure there — not even for Greaves, who is data/gyms.json town 'sanctum'. No subject wording can beat a skeleton clause that mandates buildings, so this node is routed to the new map-site class instead. That also removes the R2 violation: the previous opening, 'not a town and no houses, shops or market anywhere', was NEGATION INSIDE THE POSITIVE PROMPT on a cfg-1.0 graph. R2's finding is that the NEGATIVE conditioning is never evaluated; it is emphatically not a finding that positive-prompt negation works, and naming houses, shops and a market in positive conditioning is the surest way to summon them — R6's mechanism running in reverse. Handled by class, so nothing has to be suppressed in words. || R3 + R5 VIOLATION REMOVED — the previous 'a wide flat floor … held inside a steep dark rock wall' was a containment instruction describing a boundary enclosing the whole frame (R3) and it implicitly demanded the entire caldera bowl fit in shot, which is R5's measured failure ('seen from very high above so the whole marsh fits in the frame at once' → a rectangular causeway grid). The rock now survives only as the local FACE the gate is cut into, which is what the shipped text actually supports: prop.sanctum-approach-antler-gate 'It is set into cut rock rather than into ground.' || NINE STONES, EVENLY SPACED, ALL FACING IN — prop.sanctum-antler-ring opens verbatim: 'Nine stones at the caldera heart, evenly spaced, every one facing in toward the middle.' R1 makes the enumeration the whole lever, and the previous string threw away a shipped number and a shipped orientation by saying only 'a ring of tall grey standing stones'. Restored. || THE CARVING IS RELATIVE, NOT ABSOLUTE — same prop text: 'Each stone carries one animal on its own, cut to double the size of the figures on the stones outside.' That is double the size of the SIX-FIGURE HERD carvings on the other antler stones, a relative measure against small carvings. The previous 'at twice life size' was a fabricated absolute and would render a stag larger than the stone it is cut into. It is now 'a single antlered stag on its own, cut deep and large on the face'. Antlered stag = the Vellsire: sanctum.vellsire.approach 'The branching on its antlers is the branching cut on every stone from Meadow Reach up to here.' || THE GRASS CONTRAST IS THE ONLY VISIBLE TRACE OF THE VELLSIRE, and the previous string erased it by painting 'thin fallow grass' everywhere. Same prop text: 'The grass inside the ring is short and even. The grass elsewhere in the Sanctum Fallow stands to the knee. Inside the ring it has been grazed down level.' Both halves are now in the picture, and the contrast between them is the picture's one piece of evidence. || ISOMETRIC: nine standing stones in a ring is a composition that only works with height — in this view they read as nine verticals with the grazed circle visible between them, which is precisely the thing that has to be legible. No roof or wall material applies here; the class carries no buildings clause and none is needed. || CENTRE — this is the one node where a prop sits exactly on the spawn tile: sanctum-antler-ring (antler-stone, x512 y512, signChain vellsire-chain) IS the ring. The middle is stated positively and twice: the stones are the ring, and 'the exact middle of the picture is open grazed grass with nothing standing on it'. The footpath 'enters it through a gap between two stones' so the interior is reachable rather than a sealed pocket the player spawns into with no way out. Sourced: sanctum.vellsire.approach 'It stops in the middle of the ring, on the short grass … about a snare's throw from where the path comes in.' || floor, dry heather, dead trees — bible §6 row 6 node name 'The Sanctum Fallow'; manifest _nodes.sanctum 'a sealed caldera holding a fallow sanctum, no shops'; data/nodes/sanctum.json floraStock 50 with only carricrow-line and the Ancient vellsire-line living on it. maren.keystone.6 'fallow is a farming word. It means ground you've left to rest on purpose.' || GATE STANDING OPEN, at the bottom — adjacency ['sanctum-approach'], ONE exit, at the BOTTOM. The open gate is sourced UNCONDITIONALLY by amb.sanctum-approach-scout.base (when {}) 'That gate was already open when we got here'; maren.greeting.act6 'The gate is standing open' is act-6 gated and is corroboration only. Nothing is said about any other edge (R3); the rock is the ground the gate is cut into, not a frame boundary. || THE FINALE HAPPENS ON OPEN CALDERA FLOOR in this painting, because nothing shipped names a structure here and G2 forbids inventing one.

_versionsNote: build-doc §8.4's licensed escape, persisted: 'any asset regenerated must reuse its manifest seed unless the manifest entry is versioned'. deriveRows() reads a row's version from here, so a bump survives `rebuild` and actually moves the seed. Bump either this map or the row's own `version` field and run `rebuild` — the rebuild promotes a row-level bump into this map, clears that row's recorded seed/file (the old art is superseded, not deleted) and sets it back to pending. _img2img._source: At the handoff there was no img2img workflow: none existed, none could be retrieved, none had been trialled. The graph has since been BUILT and EXECUTED (the upload endpoint is verified and a denoise sweep ran off the approved player static), but that sweep established a LIMIT rather than an approval — img2img on this model is for deltas within a view and cannot turn one. Neither of the two uses build-doc asks for, §9.5 map year variants and §9.6 walk frames, has been run and reviewed.
_img2img._enforcement: While this is false, comfy-batch's assertSupervised() refuses any batch containing more than ONE img2img row, with or without --confirm. Set it to true only after one image has been generated through tools/comfy/img2img.ts and reviewed by a human.
